pr.title: Plan agent registration and messages between sessions
pr.head: fdb70c6cf454aabde7866699a47d573080580800

summary: Projector's watch daemon is a background process, one per machine, that writes event lines into a folder for each agent session. Projector's mod submits those lines to a Claude Code session as a prompt, and the Codex adapter queues them into a Codex thread. Today only the daemon writes there, and only about pull requests, so two agent sessions have no way to talk to each other except through you.

This pull request adds a plan, at status: ready, for a project agent command group. A session registers a name and a one-line summary, which is also how it agrees to receive messages. Another session of yours lists it and sends it a message. The message text is stored in the recipient's folder, and a one-line PEER MESSAGE event wakes the recipient, which reads the text with project agent read. That command prints a notice that the message carries none of the user's authority.

A second layer, the relay, carries the same records between machines through hidden Git refs, which point to commits outside normal branches. A user-created X25519 private key enables it and is copied between the user's machines. Records are encrypted with ChaCha20 and authenticated with HMAC-SHA256; accepting a sender also requires the user's own public key. Config commands redact the private key even when they print a containing table. Commands queue sealed records locally, and the daemon writes and pushes their Git objects in batches. This review flags missing constraints in that batching, daemon startup, Git identity, and scheduling.
The plan defers messages to other people's agents, key rotation, addressing subagents, and showing peers in Projector's panel.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Session folder. The directory under the watch state root where the daemon keeps one session's subscriptions and events.
  • Live. A registered session is live while watch.delivery reports anything but none for it. For Codex, that is while its registration lease holds.
  • Relay. The cross-machine layer: presence refs under refs/projector/agents/ and one inbox ref per message under refs/projector/inbox/, each holding one sealed record.
  • Seal. Encrypting a record with ChaCha20 and authenticating it with HMAC-SHA256, under keys agreed with X25519 between the sender's key and the recipient's public key.
  • Outbox. A per-repository file of queued ref changes, holding sealed records rather than commits, that only the daemon writes and pushes.
  • Chosen checkout. The checkout the daemon writes and pushes relay commits from: a live registered session's, or else the newest recorded one that still exists.

cards.title: Security and performance review
cards.html:
• Scope. This is a ready plan, not the implementation. The review traces its integration against the current watch daemon, Codex adapter, Git helpers, and configuration printers.
  • Earlier findings. All four earlier threads are addressed by the current plan: queue eligibility, idle liveness, writing outbox objects in the pushing checkout, and recursive secret redaction.
  • Current findings. The published review requests five plan changes: public disclosure rules, transport commit identity, cold-start registration, duplicate destination refs, and relay work blocking the shared loop.
  • Cryptography. The design includes both static and ephemeral X25519 terms, MAC verification before decryption, an own-sender-key check, recipient checks, age checks, and message-ID deduplication. Reviewing these requirements does not validate an implementation that this pull request does not contain.

groups.title: The agent messages plan
groups.kicker: One new plan: register, list, send, read, and reply, then a sealed relay across machines
intro: The plan is the only file in the change. Read § 2.1 for the commands on one machine, § 2.2 for the relay and its sealing, § 2.3 for the records and settings, and § 2.4 for the source files the build will touch. § 4 lists the acceptance tests, and § 7 splits the build into a two-layer stack, local messages first.

A message is one more event line, so watch.append_events picks the transport. The Claude mod needs no change. The Codex adapter changes only so that codex_watch.eligible keeps a line keyed to a message. The daemon's scan changes so that an idle registered agent keeps it running.

files.note: The new plan, at status: ready and priority: now.

checks.text: § 6 explicitly defers other people’s agents, key rotation, subagent addressing, and panel discovery. The ready status still requires the integration defects flagged below to be settled.
The existing Codex queue filters messages through eligible in prepare, acknowledge, drain, and dispatch. The plan now explicitly changes that common filter for message keys whose records exist.
The existing CLI prints configuration values in get/list, change_config, and report_override; the plan routes these through recursive redaction, including a whole [agent] table.
§ 2.4 permits a private repository name in a public relay message, conflicting with the supplied repository policy against putting private names in public repositories; § 3 repeats the exception.
§ 2.2 seals the tree contents but leaves Git author and committer headers unspecified. A temporary commit-tree reproduction still contained the configured login and email in both headers.

§ 2.1 does not start the daemon during registration. Existing idle Codex hooks start it only when pull-request subscriptions or queued events exist, so a first agent registration can remain unpublished.
§ 2.2 appends each change and sends one refspec per change. Two queued registrations for the same presence ref produce duplicate destinations; a temporary bare repository rejected that push.
§ 2.4 puts relay work in daemon passes. The current tick waits for each pass before Codex dispatch, and the reused Git helper has no timeout, so a slow pre-push hook can suspend unrelated delivery.

The Python suite passed at this head (1,272 tests; 108 skipped in the initial environment without Node). Project check, both plugin validations, 227 hook tests, and diff check passed. Hook type-check passed after the installed Node runtime was added to PATH.
